text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM NV said on Wednesday it intends to buy U.S. pharmaceuticals maker Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's Regensburg pharmaceutical manufacturing operations.
"The agreement will represent a new level of cooperation between DSM and Bristol-Myers Squibb, enhancing our strategic partnership," the Dutch group said in a statement.
In 1993 DSM bought the fine chemicals manufacturing part of the German pharmaceuticals plant from Bristol-Myers.
The new agreement, which is subject to due diligence, will give DSM ownership of the remaining parts of the production site, it said. No financial details were disclosed.
DSM said expansion of its ownership of the Regensburg plant and closer cooperation fitted its strategy of being a global producer of fine chemicals for the pharmaceuticals industry.
The deal, which is expected to be finalised within a few months, will also include rights to production and packaging of several products for Bristol-Myers Squibb.
